military.subtitle: Armed forces, drills, espionage, war and the nuclear program

tiles.readinessNote: Drills raise it; underfunding lowers it
tiles.moraleNote: Feeds army loyalty and coup risk

forces.fundNote: Paid from the procurement fund ({{fund}}). Queue {{queued}}/{{max}}.
forces.researchBusy: Another research project is under way.
forces.cannotAfford: The procurement fund cannot cover this.
forces.cannotOrder: Not enough in the procurement fund, or the queue is full.
forces.coveredLabel: Share of upkeep covered by the Defence budget
forces.underfunded: Underfunded: readiness and morale will decay.
forces.surplus: The surplus goes into the procurement fund.

ops.drillsNote: Exercises cost money from the procurement fund and take time, then raise readiness, morale and deterrence. At most {{max}} at once; training accidents happen.

land.label: Land exercise
land.summary: Divisions, armour and artillery train together on the northern plains.

air.label: Air exercise
air.summary: Fighter and strike squadrons practise air combat and deep strikes.

naval.label: Naval exercise
naval.summary: Fleets and submarines drill sea control and convoy defence.

joint.label: Joint exercise
joint.summary: All three services and the strategic forces rehearse a single campaign.

ops.drillBlocked: Not available: an exercise is running, two are under way, or funds are short.
ops.rivalsNote: Rival armies are hidden until a recon operation reveals them; the picture then blurs as it ages. Success depends on intelligence funding ({{efficiency}}% efficiency), your Intelligence Director {{director}} and the target’s counter-intelligence. A blown operation sours relations and causes a diplomatic incident. At most {{max}} operations at once.

recon.label: Recon
recon.summary: Reveals the target army and its readiness. The picture goes stale as time passes.

sabotage.label: Sabotage
sabotage.summary: Cripples the target’s readiness for months. Riskier: if it fails or leaves traces, there is a diplomatic incident.

counterIntel.label: Counter-intelligence
counterIntel.summary: Hunts foreign spies for four months: rival operations against India are far more likely to be caught.

war.losses: Casualties so far: India {{india}}, enemy {{enemy}}. Equipment lost: {{equipment}} units. War costs about {{cost}} a day and weighs on approval and growth.
war.capitulated_one: {{country}} has capitulated. Choose the terms of peace ({{count}} day left; reparations apply by default).
war.capitulated_other: {{country}} has capitulated. Choose the terms of peace ({{count}} days left; reparations apply by default).
war.annexNote: Annexation adds {{gdp}}% to GDP and {{population}}% to the population, but raises unrest in the {{region}} and brings three years of sanctions.

block.noWars: Wars are switched off for this game

war.peaceNote: India is not at war. A rival may attack if your deterrence is weak; you can also declare war yourself, but voters dislike wars of choice.
war.peaceNoWars: Wars are switched off for this game (New Game options): no country will attack India, and India cannot declare war.
war.declareNote: Declaring war costs {{cost}} to mobilise, hurts approval for four months and sours relations with every other country. Fighting costs money and lives every day.

confirm.approval: Approval −5 for four months, plus war weariness as the fighting drags on
confirm.relations: Relations with every other country fall
confirm.strengthUnknown: India’s strength {{india}} against their unknown army (run recon first)

nuclear.programNote: A secret program takes about {{research}} years of research, then {{enrichment}} years of enrichment, then builds a warhead every {{months}} months ({{warhead}} each). It costs {{monthly}} a month. Once it is visible to foreign services, sanctions pressure builds; the first warhead brings three years of sanctions, national pride and deterrence.

noFirstUse.label: No First Use
noFirstUse.text: India will never use nuclear weapons first. Keeps the world and voters calm; a first strike is not possible.

firstUse.label: First use reserved
firstUse.text: India reserves the right to strike first. Deterrence rises about 15%, but approval and relations with every neighbour fall.

nuclear.useNote: A nuclear strike destroys most of an enemy army and wins the war, and it also brings near-certain global sanctions for five years, a collapse in approval, unrest at home and hostile neighbours. On Hard difficulty it ends your presidency.
nuclear.changeDoctrine: Doctrine is No First Use: change it above before a first strike can be ordered.
nuclear.confirmText: You are about to use a nuclear weapon against {{country}}. This cannot be undone.

effects.sanctions: Global sanctions for five years: growth −5 pts, revenue −12%
effects.approval: Approval −25 for 18 months; unrest and terror rise nationwide
effects.hard: On Hard difficulty your presidency ends
effects.war: The enemy army is destroyed and the war ends
